resources.string: Breadbin comes with Open ROMs, a free replacement for the Commodore 64\'s BASIC, KERNAL and character set, so it works straight away. Disks, tapes, cartridges and BASIC all run on them.

Commodore\'s own ROMs are worth adding. Games of the era jump straight into the KERNAL as often as they call it, and the free ROMs are a rewrite that does not have the same code at the same addresses — so a game that halts or misbehaves on them will usually run on Commodore\'s. The KERNAL you want is revision 3, 901227-03.
VICE\'s ROM folder: basic-901226-01, kernal-901227-03, chargen-901225-01. Open one, tap Raw to download it, then add it with Choose files above.
BASIC, KERNAL, character set and the 1541 DOS, in one go

Breadbin will fetch four files from the VICE project's public repository: Commodore's BASIC 901226-01, KERNAL 901227-03 and character generator 901225-01, and the 1541's DOS.

These are Commodore's firmware from 1982 and 1983. They are still under copyright, nobody has ever released them, and they have been carried by emulator projects for about thirty years without anyone objecting. Whether you may use them is your call.

The 1541 DOS arrives switched off — turn it on for fast loaders.
The same project\'s drive ROM folder. Optional — disks load without it.

Paste the address of a ROM file and Breadbin will fetch it and work out which of the three it is. Breadbin does not come with an address: where you get the ROMs, and whether you may, is yours to decide.

The program has stopped the processor.\n\nGames of this era often jump straight into the KERNAL rather than calling it, and the free ROMs are a rewrite that does not have the same code in the same places. Adding Commodore\'s own KERNAL in Settings usually fixes it.

This game jumps into the KERNAL at $%1$s.

That is inside the KERNAL rather than one of its published entry points, so it is Commodore's own code there and the middle of something unrelated in the free replacement. The game will misbehave, and may stop altogether.

Get Commodore's ROMs in Settings and it should run properly.

The program has stopped the processor, after jumping into the KERNAL at $%1$s.

That address is inside the KERNAL rather than one of its published entry points, so it holds Commodore's own code and something else entirely in the free replacement. This is the usual reason a game of this era stops dead.

Get Commodore's ROMs in Settings and it will very likely run.
That file is no longer in the library.
Types the LOAD and RUN for you when a disk or program is opened.
Go back to the free ROMs
Breadbin is a Commodore 64 emulator. No ads, no tracking, no accounts. The only thing that ever opens a connection is the ROM import, and only when you type an address into it yourself.
